markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **recent-support residual SASRec trained with sampled cross-entropy**. Its benefits remain hypotheses pending pinned macro validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already learns history weighting; an explicit recent branch therefore needs incremental-value controls. User feedback suggests broad historical associations sometimes overwhelm specific intent. (2) Electronics has 14.95% wrong sampled-pair rankings and −0.4812 margin p10. These identify separation problems, not top-10 generalization. (3) Embedding similarity scores of 0.5392–0.5566 provide little evidence of severe collapse. Intent selection and supervision deserve priority over diversity regularization.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Turning Dross Into Gold motivates sampled cross-entropy with negatives shared within each sequence. Its reported 3,000 negatives do not establish an optimum here. (2) TLSRec and HAM motivate short/long-term fusion and recent pooling. Neither establishes gains beyond SASRec here. (3) ReZero motivates an initially zero residual that preserves baseline scores. R2NS supports postponing hard mining because hard negatives may be unobserved positives.

**Framework and directions.** Three axes organize interventions: evidence selection, ranking supervision, and directional relationships. SASRec supplies causal historical evidence; recent pooling selects local evidence; sampled cross-entropy strengthens candidate competition; transition residuals add directional association. None establishes equipment compatibility, ownership, or satisfied needs. Sampled HR@10 evaluates the pinned candidate protocol, not full-catalog recommendation quality [Krichene–Rendle].

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension includes a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Uniform sampled cross-entropy [Dross] | 2/7/4/9/3 | O: reproducible; established. P: scalable; benchmark dependent. U: sharper competition; no explicit recency. M: targets separation; diagnostic margins may not generalize. D: small loss change; sampling requires care. |
| Recent residual + sampled cross-entropy [Dross, HAM, ReZero] | 3/7/8/8/5 | O: diagnosis-guided combination; familiar components. P: extensible; benefit beyond SASRec uncertain. U: targets stale and broad matches; cannot verify compatibility. M: targets confusion; extra capacity can overfit. D: compact branch; causal pooling and predictor parity require care. |
| Shrunk directed-transition residual [GaGNN] | 5/7/7/6/5 | O: asymmetric evidence; established graph concept. P: interpretable; rare edges unreliable. U: specific next-step support; association is not practical fit. M: candidate separation; popularity can dominate. D: sparse counts; causal construction adds work. |

**Selected algorithm.** Pool the last five nonpadding observed embeddings at each causal position. Set z = h + sigmoid(gate(h,r))·Wᵣr; initialize Wᵣ and its bias to zero, preserve existing SASRec normalization, and verify identical initial evaluation scores. Train with 64 unique uniform eligible negatives per sequence, reused at all valid positions. Exclude padding and every training-history item; use fewer negatives only when the eligible catalog is smaller. This candidate-classification objective uses ordinary cross-entropy without LogQ correction; it is not an unbiased full-softmax approximation.

The residual targets stale/isolated-history influence and broad matches lacking recent support; the loss targets weak separation. These are mechanisms to test, not established resolutions. Compare unchanged SASRec, objective-only, fusion-only, and combined variants. Predeclare checkpoint cadence and tie rules; preserve all routes, seeds, splits, diagnostic interfaces, and predictor parity. Select only by pinned macro HR@10, report category results and paired uncertainty, and account for every trial within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Additional shortcut controls and exact reproduction rules appear in implementation notes.

idea.description: Recent-support residual SASRec with sequence-shared uniform sampled cross-entropy. Add a baseline-preserving, gated mean of recent item embeddings to causal SASRec features, and train next-item classification against multiple eligible alternatives.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies two eligible targets: stale or isolated interactions being treated as current demand, and broad similarity producing recommendations without specific recent support. Recent pooling provides an explicit local-evidence path, while a learned gate permits the existing history representation to remain dominant. The model diagnosis identifies weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics' 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative margin p10; multi-negative cross-entropy addresses candidate discrimination. SASRec already models recency, so additional benefit must be demonstrated. Neither mechanism establishes compatibility, confirmed ownership, replacement demand, or satisfaction of a durable-device need; uncertain recommendations must remain distinct from explicit mismatches.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, original splits, and trial-local artifacts. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS, whose supplied default is 200. Do not download weights or datasets. Only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps are eligible; ignore the generic examples listing unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, or stores. Simulator diversity and conformity traits remain unobserved.

Architecture: retain the original SASRec encoder, item embeddings, positional representation, normalization, and scoring scale. Let h_t be its original output and r_t the masked mean of the embeddings for observed positions max(1,t−4) through t. Exclude padding and return zero for an empty window. Use g_t = sigmoid(aᵀ concat(h_t,r_t) + b), with a initialized to zero and b = −2. Set z_t = h_t + g_t * (W_r r_t + c_r), initializing W_r and c_r to zero. Add no post-fusion LayerNorm. This produces exactly the original features at initialization; verify matching evaluation-mode scores with identical backbone weights and branch enabled versus disabled. Do not zero both the gate output and projection, which would block learning. The projection can learn immediately; gate parameters begin learning after the projection becomes nonzero. Pool only observed inputs through t; the shifted target at t+1 never enters r_t.

Sampling and loss: build each user's exclusion set from the complete available training history, including shifted training targets. Never inspect held-out interactions for exclusions. For each sampled sequence, draw K_u = min(64, number_of_eligible_items) unique uniform negatives without replacement from IDs 1..item_count outside that exclusion set. Reuse that sequence's negatives at all valid timesteps; refresh them on the next training draw. Use rejection sampling with a local seeded generator and an explicit eligible-list fallback when acceptance becomes inefficient. Skip and log sequences with no eligible negatives. Score the positive in column zero and that sequence's negatives in the remaining columns; average ordinary cross-entropy over nonpadding target positions. Unique sampling avoids accidental duplicate weighting in the denominator. This defines sampled candidate classification, not an unbiased estimate of unrestricted full-catalog softmax. No LogQ correction is part of this chosen objective. Chunk score computation while preserving the global valid-position mean and gradients. Keep backbone hyperparameters, optimizer, regularization, batch size, sequence length, training sampler, and learning-rate schedule identical to the supplied baseline unless explicitly registered as a separate trial.

Evaluation and budget: predeclare four primary configurations—unchanged SASRec, objective-only, fusion-only using the original BCE, and combined—and use identical checkpoint cadence, for example every 10 completed epochs through the configured limit. Establish equal per-configuration GPU-time caps before execution, reserving measured validation and diagnosis costs within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; all failed trials count. Record completed epochs and updates because equal GPU time can mean unequal optimization steps. Select checkpoints and complete four-route configurations exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. For exact ties, prefer the simpler configuration, then the earlier checkpoint, then a fixed configuration order. Report neighboring evaluated checkpoints, category HR values, elapsed GPU time, failures, and the complete selection record. Do not claim that an unexecuted configuration completed or improved results.

If the budget permits, prioritize a fixed-gate recent-mean control and a last-item residual to test whether learned fusion improves on a recency shortcut. Further registered controls are full-history mean, a training-frequency popularity-only score adjustment, and window sizes 1/5/10. A normalization-only control becomes necessary if normalization is changed. These are optional experiments, not required evidence already obtained. Avoid a broad adaptive search over them. Report head/tail slices using a predeclared cutoff derived only from training frequencies, with slice sample sizes; they are diagnostic and do not replace the macro selection metric.

Where the pinned evaluator exposes per-user hits, retain paired candidate and baseline hits for the same 200 users/category and fixed candidate sets. Use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with a separate analysis RNG seed 42: independently resample paired users within each category, compute each category's mean hit difference, and equally average the four differences. Report the observed macro difference, percentile 95% interval, and category differences. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. The interval conditions on the trained models and fixed candidates; it excludes training randomness, candidate variability, and adaptive selection optimism. If per-user outputs are unavailable, report that limitation rather than modifying the host evaluator or inventing intervals. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog quality.

Serialization and diagnostics: update both checkpoint configuration and the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the pooling, gate, projection, and category routing exactly. Save window size, backbone configuration, item mappings, and state_dict beneath the trial directory. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and their definitions. view.model must be the actual trained module; view.item_emb remains its item table, view.log2feats returns z, and view.predict_score performs the actual shared-embedding scoring. Preserve the supplied margin and embedding-similarity definitions and diagnostic sampling procedure for comparability. Category breakdowns must be explicitly unavailable, not inferred or fabricated. Diagnostics use training data only and remain separate from selection. Twenty real training users, five/category, still receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations through the native simulator. Preserve qualitative distinctions between immediate choice, conditional appeal, explicit mismatch, and uncertainty; do not manufacture numeric simulator acceptance or trait measurements.
idea.pseudocode:
register primary_configs = [baseline, objective_only, fusion_only, combined]
register checkpoint_cadence, tie_rules, GPU_time_caps, baseline_hyperparameters
for configuration in primary_configs:
    for category in four_categories:
        initialize baseline backbone using prescribed seed 42
        if fusion_enabled:
            initialize gate_weights=0, gate_bias=-2
            initialize recent_projection_weight=0, recent_projection_bias=0
            verify initial eval scores match the same backbone without fusion
        for epoch in configured_epochs subject to registered GPU-time cap:
            for user_ids, sequence, positive, original_negative in baseline_batches:
                h = original_causal_sasrec(sequence)
                if fusion_enabled:
                    r = causal_nonpadding_embedding_mean(sequence, window=5)
                    g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r)))
                    z = h + g * recent_projection(r)
                else:
                    z = h
                if sampled_CE_enabled:
                    for user in batch:
                        eligible = catalog_ids_without_padding - complete_training_history[user]
                        K_user = min(64, len(eligible))
                        negatives[user] = uniform_unique_sample(eligible, K_user)
                    logits = positive_and_sequence_shared_negative_scores(z)
                    loss = summed_CE_over_valid_targets_with_eligible_negatives / valid_target_count
                else:
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(z, positive, original_negative)
                optimizer_step(loss)
            at registered checkpoints:
                obtain pinned validation macro and category HR10 without altering evaluator
                log checkpoint, updates, GPU_time, and available paired user hits
        save routed model configuration, weights, and matching predictor beneath trial
select completed eligible configuration/checkpoint using registered macro-HR10 and tie rules
report all trials, category results, checkpoint neighborhoods, and conditional paired uncertainty if available
run required training-only diagnostics using actual fused features
leave held-out test evaluation to host

originality.positive: The combination is tied explicitly to current-intent failures and weak candidate separation, with controls distinguishing the two mechanisms.
originality.negative: Recent mean pooling, gated residual fusion, zero-initialized residuals, and sampled cross-entropy are established techniques; their combination offers limited methodological novelty.

future_potential.positive: A small residual provides a practical platform for studying when local evidence improves an existing sequential model, with inexpensive component ablations.
future_potential.negative: SASRec already adapts history weighting, and the residual may merely learn a last-item or popularity shortcut. Missing compatibility information limits the user-facing failures it can resolve.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture adds only masked pooling, a scalar gate, and a linear projection while preserving the backbone and scoring interface.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable implementation also requires sequence-specific sampling, variable eligible counts, baseline-preserving initialization, predictor parity, budget accounting, and comparable diagnostics.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides causal self-attention and shared item scoring.
Already adapts attention across recent and longer-term interactions, establishing the need for controls on any added recent branch.
limitations: The supplied user diagnosis indicates failures of specific current-intent matching, but does not establish which SASRec component causes them.

related_work.title: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Studies full-catalog and uncorrected sampled cross-entropy as alternatives to one-negative BCE.
Samples negatives per user sequence and shares them across valid timesteps; reports strong results with 3,000 negatives.
limitations: Does not establish that 64 negatives or this architecture improves the pinned benchmark.
The supplied evidence does not verify repository duplicate-handling behavior; unique negatives are an explicit choice here.

related_work.title: TLSRec
contributions: Motivates regulating short- and long-term preference contributions using temporal evidence.
limitations: The selected branch uses sequence order rather than timestamp features and is not a reproduction of TLSRec.
An unknown next-interaction timestamp cannot be used.

related_work.title: HAM
contributions: Provides precedent for mean pooling recent interactions and evidence that learned attention is not consistently necessary.
limitations: Does not establish the value of a learned gate or a five-item window on this benchmark.

related_work.title: ReZero Is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Motivates zero-initialized residual contributions that preserve initial network behavior.
limitations: The zero-projection gated branch is an adaptation of the initialization principle, not a directly validated recommendation method.

related_work.title: GaGNN
contributions: Motivates supplementing sparse histories with individual and group transition relationships.
limitations: Chronological associations do not prove equipment compatibility or product complementarity.
Sparse transition edges and popularity effects require shrinkage and separate validation.

related_work.title: R2NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up before progressively harder negative sampling.
limitations: Hard candidates can be unobserved positives; the initial selected experiment therefore retains uniform sampling.

related_work.title: LogQ analysis for sampled recommendation objectives
contributions: Highlights the distinction between deterministic positive inclusion and sampled negatives when correcting sampled objectives.
limitations: Uniform sampling alone does not make an uncorrected candidate-classification loss an unbiased full-catalog softmax approximation.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the mandated benchmark as a selection target; it limits claims about full-catalog recommendation quality.

related_work.title: Cañamares et al., statistical comparisons in recommendation
contributions: Supports user-level statistical comparisons of recommendation performance.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified paired bootstrap is a task-specific analysis and does not correct adaptive model-selection optimism.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation data.
limitations: Predeclared comparisons and checkpoint rules reduce researcher flexibility but do not eliminate selection bias.

related_work.title: Are We Really Making Much Progress? A Worrying Analysis of Recent Neural Recommendation Approaches
contributions: Motivates reproducible baselines, controlled comparisons, and transparent tuning records.
limitations: Does not establish gains for any proposed component under the pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: Recency-sampling research
contributions: Motivates separating improvements from recency handling from improvements attributed to richer fusion.
limitations: The supplied search evidence does not establish a matching result for this residual architecture or candidate protocol.
